messages:
evalbot: NIGHTLY_EVAL ALERT — run 2026-03-19T03:00Z. Multiple suites failed for model rw-13b-v2-int4. Failing suites: instruct-qa (accuracy down 6%), long-context-consistency (coherence down 9%), generation-quality (short hallucinations increased). Link: https://console.redwood.ai/evals/2026-03-19/2391234567 :rotating_light:

maria: saw this in my inbox, thanks for the ping. initial severity? P1/P2? :eyes:

oliver: based on % drops I'd call this P2 for now, but if customers report production impact escalate. no incidents reported yet.

jessica: any recent model or quant rollout last night?

samir: I rolled int4 kernel set v2.1 to Dedicated and Hosted canaries at 01:10Z. small batch of hosts (10%) got the kernels. not aware of full rollout.

maria: ok assigning owners: @samir to investigate runtime/quant changes, @jessica to triage eval artifacts and gather failing prompts/samples. samir/jessica please update here with initial findings in 30m.

samir: will check kernel diff + kernel logs. first quick check: compare logits distribution between fp16 and int4 reproducer. running reproducer locally now.

jessica: I'm grabbing failing samples and will run the eval locally against rw-13b-v2 (fp16) and rw-13b-v2-int4 to produce side-by-side outputs. will paste a few examples here.

kevin: tagging infra — if this is quant kernel regression we should check canary vs stable routing. i can verify traffic split and rollback toggle.

samir: quick repro command (local):

```
python -m rw_eval.run --model rw-13b-v2-int4 --suite instruct-qa --seed 42 --batch 8 --max-tokens 256 --log-preds /tmp/int4_preds.json
python -m rw_eval.run --model rw-13b-v2 --suite instruct-qa --seed 42 --batch 8 --max-tokens 256 --log-preds /tmp/fp16_preds.json
diff -u /tmp/fp16_preds.json /tmp/int4_preds.json | head -n 60
```

jessica: sample failing prompt 1 (from cohort A):
"You are given a list of ingredients, produce a step-by-step allergen-safe recipe."
FP16 answer: lists safe substitutions and steps (correct).
INT4 answer: fabricates an ingredient "silk flour" and skips steps.

samir: noted hallucination pattern on substitution tokens. initial hypothesis: quantized kernel rounding on embedding projection for low-frequency tokens. will dump embedding norms next.

maria: for severity/triage: mark as P2 for now, but set on-call watch and hold any further int4 rollouts until owners confirm.

jessica: grabbing eval diffs now. preliminary: 14% of failing cases are hallucination-like, 70% are coherence regressions on longer contexts. saving full CSV to https://s3.redwood.ai/evals/alerts/2391234567/diffs.csv

samir: kernel logs show increased perf, no OOMs. attaching snippet of kernel diff id 9c4f: "quant-rounding-adjustment: enabled" — maybe that change altered low-rank projections. pinging @maria for rollback permission.

maria: approve rollback for the canary hosts. kevin, can you flip the toggle for the 10% group and re-run nightly at 03:10Z?

kevin: on it. will rollback canary to kernel v2.0 and re-trigger the nightly eval job. I'll post status. :gear:

deploybot: Canary rollback to v2.0 started for pool 'dedicated-canary' at 03:22Z.

samir: I'll keep investigating embedding norms and run targeted tests for low-frequency tokens. if we confirm regression caused by rounding change we'll revert the rounding tweak and re-run quant CI.

jessica: after rollback results: early re-run (subset) looks closer to fp16 — hallucination rate cut by ~60% on sample set. will run full nightly once rollback completes.

maria: good work. owners: samir (runtime/quant fix) and jessica (eval regressions + report). oliver to monitor customer reports. kevin to confirm full rollback and nightly re-run. please update thread when you have reproducer diff and recommended fix.

evalbot: Incident created INC-2026-342 with owners samir,jessica. Notifications sent to oncall and customers flagged for impacted models.

samir: initial timeline estimate: root cause analysis 2-4h, patch + CI 4-8h depending on replication. will aim for hotfix if trivial revert.

jessica: will prepare a short summary doc with reproducible examples and evaluation diffs for postmortem.

maria: thanks team — stand by for updates. :thumbsup:
